subject: maths
title: Measuring Angles: Acute, Obtuse and Reflex Angles, Protractors and Regular Polygons
seo_title: Year 5 Measuring Angles Worksheets: Protractor, Reflex Angles, 180° and 360° (Free, with Answers)
standard_text: Know angles are measured in degrees: estimate and compare acute, obtuse and reflex angles; draw given angles, and measure them in degrees (°); identify: angles at a point and one whole turn (total 360°), angles at a point on a straight line and ½ a turn (total 180°), other multiples of 90°; distinguish between regular and irregular polygons based on reasoning about equal sides and angles.
meta_desc: Free Year 5 maths worksheets on measuring angles: acute, obtuse and reflex angles, estimating, reading a protractor, angles on a straight line and around a point, turns, and regular and irregular polygons. 100 questions with an answer key, following the National Curriculum.
key_big: A whole turn is 360°, a straight line is 180° and a right angle is 90°. Reflex angles are more than 180°.
key_sub: On a protractor, put the centre on the vertex, line up one arm with 0 and read the scale that starts at that 0. Estimate first so you can spot a reading from the wrong scale.
body_html:
Types of angle

An angle is an amount of turn. We measure it in degrees (°). A whole turn is 360°, half a turn is 180° and a quarter turn is 90°, a right angle.

TypeSize
Acuteless than 90°
Right angleexactly 90°
Obtusemore than 90°, less than 180°
Reflexmore than 180°, less than 360°

To estimate, compare with a right angle (90°) and a straight line (180°). The length of the arms does not change the size of the angle.

Measure with a protractor

1. Put the centre of the protractor on the vertex. 2. Line up one arm with 0. 3. Read the scale that starts at 0 on that arm. 4. Check with your estimate: acute or obtuse?

Draw an angle of 65°

Draw a line. Put the centre on one end and the line on 0.

Count along the scale that starts at 0 on your line to 65, make a dot, and join it to the end of the line.

Answer: an angle of 65°

Reflex angle

The angle on the other side measures 130°. Find the reflex angle.

The two angles make a whole turn: 360° − 130° = 230°.

Answer: 230°

Straight lines, points and turns

Missing angle

Two angles on a straight line are 55° and ?. Find ?.

180° − 55° = 125°. Check: 55° + 125° = 180°.

Answer: 125°

Regular and irregular polygons

A polygon is regular if all its sides are equal and all its angles are equal. If either is not true, it is irregular. Small marks show which sides and angles are equal.

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Reading the wrong scale (140° for a 40° angle)Read the scale that starts at 0 on your arm, then check your estimate
Calling 190° obtuseObtuse is between 90° and 180°. More than 180° is reflex
Using 180° for a whole turnStraight line: 180°. All the way round: 360°
Thinking longer arms make a bigger angleThe size of an angle is the amount of turn, not the length of the arms
Saying a shape is regular because its sides are equalRegular needs equal sides and equal angles

faq.q: What do Year 5 children learn about angles?
faq.a: They learn to name acute, obtuse and reflex angles, estimate and measure angles with a protractor, draw angles, use angles on a straight line (180°) and around a point (360°), and tell regular from irregular polygons.

faq.q: How do you teach measuring angles with a protractor in Year 5?
faq.a: Estimate first. Then put the centre on the vertex, line up one arm with 0 and read the scale that starts at that 0. Check the reading against the estimate.
A reflex angle is more than 180° and less than 360°. To measure one, measure the angle on the other side and subtract it from 360°.

faq.q: What is the difference between a regular and an irregular polygon?
faq.a: A regular polygon has all sides equal and all angles equal, like a square. A rectangle and a rhombus are irregular, because only their angles or only their sides are equal.

items.e: An obtuse angle is bigger than a right angle but smaller than a straight line: between 90° and 180°. This angle is 125°.

items.q: Which of these angles is reflex?
items.e: A reflex angle is more than 180°. Only 210° is more than 180°. 175° is close to 180°, but it is still obtuse.

items.q: An angle measures 89°. What type of angle is it?
items.e: An acute angle is smaller than a right angle. 89° is less than 90° (only just!).

items.q: Jack says an angle of 190° is obtuse because it is bigger than 90°. Is he right?
c: No, it is a right angle
items.e: Obtuse angles are bigger than 90° but smaller than 180°. 190° is more than 180°, so it is reflex.

A reflex angle is bigger than a straight line: between 180° and 360°. Look at the arc: it goes round the outside. This angle is 320°. (The angle on the other side is 40°, but the arc marks the big angle.)

items.q: What type of angle is marked?
items.e: A right angle is exactly 90°, a quarter turn. The small square shows it. This angle is 90°. Turning the angle does not change its size.

A reflex angle is bigger than a straight line: between 180° and 360°. Look at the arc: it goes round the outside. This angle is 200°. (The angle on the other side is 160°, but the arc marks the big angle.)

items.q: A reflex angle is …
items.e: Reflex angles are bigger than a half turn (180°) but smaller than a whole turn (360°).

items.q: What type of angle is marked?
items.e: An acute angle is smaller than a right angle: less than 90°. This angle is 70°.
Two arms that make a straight line make an angle of 180°, half a turn. This angle is 180°.

A reflex angle is bigger than a straight line: between 180° and 360°. Look at the arc: it goes round the outside. This angle is 230°. (The angle on the other side is 130°, but the arc marks the big angle.)

items.q: An angle measures 270°. What type of angle is it?
items.e: A reflex angle is bigger than a straight line. 270° is more than 180° but less than 360°.

items.q: An angle measures 185°. What type of angle is it?
items.e: A reflex angle is bigger than a straight line. 185° is more than 180° but less than 360°.

items.q: At which time is the smaller angle between the hands of a clock acute?
items.e: At 1 o’clock the hands are 1 hour space apart: 30°, which is acute. 3 o’clock is a right angle (90°), 4 o’clock is obtuse (120°) and 6 o’clock is a straight line (180°).

items.q: Which of these angles is obtuse?
items.e: An obtuse angle is between 90° and 180°. 135° is the only one. 225° is more than 180°, so it is reflex.
An obtuse angle is bigger than a right angle but smaller than a straight line: between 90° and 180°. This angle is 100°.

items.q: An angle measures 175°. What type of angle is it?
items.e: An obtuse angle is bigger than a right angle but smaller than a straight line. 175° is more than 90° but less than 180°.

items.q: Which list goes from the smallest angle to the largest?
items.e: Acute is less than 90°, a right angle is 90°, obtuse is between 90° and 180°, and reflex is more than 180°.
An obtuse angle is bigger than a right angle but smaller than a straight line: between 90° and 180°. This angle is 160°.

items.q: What type of angle is marked?
items.e: An acute angle is smaller than a right angle: less than 90°. This angle is 35°.

items.q: Aisha estimates a reflex angle as about 70°. Why must she be wrong?
c: 70° is too big for any angle
A reflex angle is more than 180°
A reflex angle is less than 90°
items.e: Every reflex angle is more than 180°, so its estimate must be more than 180°. 70° may be the angle on the other side: then the reflex angle is about 360° − 70° = 290°.

items.q: Which is the best estimate for the marked angle?
items.e: The angle is smaller than a right angle (90°), so it is acute. About 60° fits. (It is 62°.) About 120° would be a much wider angle.
The arc goes round the outside, so the angle is reflex: more than 180°. The angle on the other side is about 60°, so the marked angle is about 360° − 60° = 300°. (It is 300°.)
Obtuse means between 90° and 180°. D is about 145°. B is reflex: the gap between its arms looks obtuse, but the arc marks the angle round the outside.

items.q: Which is the best estimate for the marked angle?
items.e: The angle is smaller than a right angle (90°), so it is acute. About 30° fits. (It is 28°.) About 150° would be a much wider angle.
A reflex angle is more than 180°. Only the arc in D goes round more than a straight line. A is obtuse, nearly 180°.
The arc goes round the outside, so the angle is reflex: more than 180°. The angle on the other side is about 160°, so the marked angle is about 360° − 160° = 200°. (It is 205°.)
The angle is bigger than a right angle (90°) but smaller than a straight line (180°), so it is obtuse. About 120° fits. (It is 118°.) About 60° would be a much smaller angle.
The size of an angle is the amount of turn, not the length of the arms. A is reflex (about 250°), so it is the largest, even though its arms are the shortest.

items.q: An angle is a little smaller than a right angle. Which could it be?
items.e: A right angle is 90°. A little smaller than 90° is about 80°. 100° is a little bigger.

items.q: An angle is a little more than half a turn. Which could it be?
items.e: Half a turn is 180°, so a little more is about 195°. 165° is a little less than half a turn, and 95° is a little more than a quarter turn.
The arc goes round the outside, so the angle is reflex: more than 180°. The angle on the other side is about 90°, so the marked angle is about 360° − 90° = 270°. (It is 275°.)
The angle is bigger than a right angle (90°) but smaller than a straight line (180°), so it is obtuse. About 150° fits. (It is 147°.) About 30° would be a much smaller angle.

items.q: Which is the best estimate for the marked angle?
items.e: The angle is smaller than a right angle (90°), so it is acute. About 45° fits. (It is 43°.) About 135° would be a much wider angle.

items.q: Which angle is closest to 45°?
items.e: 45° is half a right angle. B is about half of a right angle. A is nearly a right angle, C is very small and D is obtuse.

items.q: Which list goes from the smallest angle to the largest?
items.e: Compare the hundreds, then the tens: 59° < 95° < 185° < 205°.
C is a bit more than a right angle: about 120°. A is about 60°. B is reflex (about 240°): its inside gap looks like 120°, but the arc marks the big angle. D is nearly a straight line.
The angle is bigger than a right angle (90°) but smaller than a straight line (180°), so it is obtuse. About 170° fits. (It is 172°.) About 10° would be a much smaller angle.
The arc goes round the outside, so the angle is reflex: more than 180°. The angle on the other side is about 120°, so the marked angle is about 360° − 120° = 240°. (It is 235°.)

items.q: Which is larger: three right angles or 250°?
items.e: Three right angles are 3 × 90° = 270°, and 270° is more than 250°.

sets.title: Measure and draw angles with a protractor

items.q: To find a reflex angle, Ava measures the angle on the other side. It is 130°. What is the reflex angle?
items.e: The two angles go all the way round the vertex, so they add up to 360°. 360° − 130° = 230°. (50° comes from using 180° instead of 360°.)

items.q: What is the size of the angle?
items.e: The bottom arm is on 0 on the right, so read the inner scale, which starts at 0 on the right. The other arm crosses it at 110. The outer scale says 70 there, but it starts from the other side. The angle is bigger than a right angle, so 110° makes sense.

items.q: Neither arm is on 0. What is the size of the angle?
items.e: On the inner scale one arm is at 20 and the other is at 95. The angle is the difference: 95° − 20° = 75°.

items.q: What is the size of the angle?
items.e: The bottom arm is on 0 on the right, so read the inner scale, which starts at 0 on the right. The other arm crosses it at 135. The small marks go up in 5s, so the mark between 130 and 140 is 135. The outer scale says 45 there, but it starts from the other side. The angle is bigger than a right angle, so 135° makes sense.

items.q: What is the size of the angle?
items.e: The bottom arm is on 0 on the left, so read the outer scale, which starts at 0 on the left. The other arm crosses it at 55. The small marks go up in 5s, so the mark between 50 and 60 is 55. (The inner scale says 125 there.) The angle is smaller than a right angle, so 55° makes sense.

items.q: What is the size of the angle?
items.e: The bottom arm is on 0 on the left, so read the outer scale, which starts at 0 on the left. The other arm crosses it at 100. (The inner scale says 80 there.) The angle is bigger than a right angle, so 100° makes sense.

items.q: Maya wants to draw an angle of 65°. She puts her line on 0 of the inner scale. Where should she make a mark?
items.e: Use the scale that starts at 0 on your line: the inner scale. Count up to 65 (the small mark between 60 and 70), make a dot, then join it to the vertex. The small marks go up in 5s, so 5 marks after 60 would be 85. On the outer scale, 65 would give 115°.

items.q: What is the size of the angle?
items.e: The bottom arm is on 0 on the right, so read the inner scale, which starts at 0 on the right. The other arm crosses it at 65. The small marks go up in 5s, so the mark between 60 and 70 is 65. The outer scale says 115 there, but it starts from the other side. The angle is smaller than a right angle, so 65° makes sense.

items.q: What is the size of the angle?
items.e: The bottom arm is on 0 on the right, so read the inner scale, which starts at 0 on the right. The other arm crosses it at 80. The outer scale says 100 there, but it starts from the other side. The angle is smaller than a right angle, so 80° makes sense.

items.q: Oliver measures an angle that is clearly smaller than a right angle. The arm crosses the protractor at 35 and 145. What is the angle?
items.e: An angle smaller than a right angle is less than 90°, so it is 35°. 145 is on the other scale.

items.q: What is the size of the angle?
items.e: The bottom arm is on 0 on the left, so read the outer scale, which starts at 0 on the left. The other arm crosses it at 145. The small marks go up in 5s, so the mark between 140 and 150 is 145. (The inner scale says 35 there.) The angle is bigger than a right angle, so 145° makes sense.

items.q: What is the size of the angle?
items.e: The bottom arm is on 0 on the left, so read the outer scale, which starts at 0 on the left. The other arm crosses it at 30. (The inner scale says 150 there.) The angle is smaller than a right angle, so 30° makes sense.

items.q: A protractor only goes to 180°. How can you draw a reflex angle of 250°?
c: Draw 70°, then mark the angle outside it
Draw 110°, then mark the angle outside it
items.e: 360° − 250° = 110°. Draw an angle of 110°. The angle round the outside is then 250°. (250° − 180° = 70° is a different angle.)

items.q: Neither arm is on 0. What is the size of the angle?
items.e: On the inner scale one arm is at 40 and the other is at 150. The angle is the difference: 150° − 40° = 110°.

items.q: What is the size of the angle?
items.e: The bottom arm is on 0 on the left, so read the outer scale, which starts at 0 on the left. The other arm crosses it at 70. (The inner scale says 110 there.) The angle is smaller than a right angle, so 70° makes sense.

items.q: What is the size of the angle?
items.e: The bottom arm is on 0 on the left, so read the outer scale, which starts at 0 on the left. The other arm crosses it at 120. (The inner scale says 60 there.) The angle is bigger than a right angle, so 120° makes sense.

items.q: What is the size of the angle?
items.e: The bottom arm is on 0 on the right, so read the inner scale, which starts at 0 on the right. The other arm crosses it at 40. The outer scale says 140 there, but it starts from the other side. The angle is smaller than a right angle, so 40° makes sense.

items.q: One arm of an angle is on 0 of the outer scale. Which scale should you read?
c: the scale with the bigger number
the scale with the smaller number
items.e: Read the scale that starts at 0 on your arm. Here that is the outer scale.

items.q: What is the size of the angle?
items.e: The bottom arm is on 0 on the right, so read the inner scale, which starts at 0 on the right. The other arm crosses it at 155. The small marks go up in 5s, so the mark between 150 and 160 is 155. The outer scale says 25 there, but it starts from the other side. The angle is bigger than a right angle, so 155° makes sense.

items.q: Where do you put the centre of the protractor when you measure an angle?
c: at the end of an arm
in the middle of an arm
items.e: The centre goes on the vertex, where the two arms meet. Then line up one arm with 0.

sets.title: Angles on a straight line, around a point and turns

items.e: Angles around a point add up to 360°. The three angles are equal: 360° ÷ 3 = 120°. (60° comes from 180° ÷ 3.)
The line is tilted, but it is still straight: 180° − 140° = 40°. (220° would be for angles around a point.)

items.q: Amelia faces south and turns 270° clockwise. Which way does she face now?
items.e: 270° is 3 right angles. Clockwise from south: west (90°), north (180°), east (270°). (West would be a quarter turn clockwise, or 270° anticlockwise.)

items.q: Angles on a straight line add up to …
items.e: A straight line is half a turn: 180°. Two right angles make a straight line.

items.q: One whole turn is …
items.e: A whole turn goes all the way round: 360°. It is 4 right angles: 4 × 90° = 360°.

items.q: How many right angles make a whole turn?
items.e: 4 × 90° = 360°, so 4 right angles make a whole turn. 2 right angles make a straight line.

items.q: How many degrees are in a half turn?
items.e: A whole turn is 360°, and half of 360° is 180°.

items.q: What do two right angles make?
items.e: 2 × 90° = 180°, half a turn. The arms make a straight line. 4 right angles make a whole turn.

items.q: The angles are on a straight line. Work out the missing angle.
items.e: First add the angles you know: 40° + 55° = 95°. Then 180° − 95° = 85°.
Angles on a straight line add up to 180°. 180° − 55° = 125°.

items.q: Which angle is a multiple of 90°?
Alfie faces north and turns clockwise to face east. How many degrees does he turn?
items.e: North to east clockwise is a quarter turn: 90°.
The two angles go all the way around the point: 360°. 360° − 70° = 290°, a reflex angle. (110° comes from using 180°.)

items.q: How many degrees are in a three-quarter turn?
items.e: A quarter turn is 90°. Three quarter turns are 3 × 90° = 270°. (75° is three quarters of 100, but a turn is 360°.)

items.q: Ruby faces north and turns anticlockwise until she faces east. How many degrees does she turn?
items.e: Anticlockwise from north: west (90°), south (180°), then east (270°). It is the long way round. (90° would be clockwise.)

items.q: The angles are on a straight line. Work out the missing angle.
items.e: The small square is a right angle: 90°. 90° + 62° = 152°, and 180° − 152° = 28°.

items.q: How many right angles are there in 270°?
items.e: 270° ÷ 90° = 3. Three right angles make a three-quarter turn.
Angles around a point add up to 360°. 120° + 140° = 260°, and 360° − 260° = 100°.
360° − 90° = 270° is left for the two equal angles. 270° ÷ 2 = 135°. (45° comes from using 180°.)

items.q: Is this pentagon regular or irregular?
c: Irregular: the angles are not all equal
Irregular: the sides and the angles are not all equal
Regular: all sides and all angles are equal
Irregular: the sides are not all equal
items.e: There are no equal marks. The sides are clearly different lengths and the angles are different sizes, so it is irregular.

items.q: How many degrees does the minute hand of a clock turn in 15 minutes?
items.e: 60 minutes is a whole turn (360°). 15 minutes is a quarter of an hour, so a quarter turn: 90°.

items.q: What is the smaller angle between the hands of the clock at 4 o’clock?
items.e: The 12 hour spaces go around 360°, so each is 360° ÷ 12 = 30°. At 4 o’clock the hands are 4 spaces apart: 4 × 30° = 120°.

items.q: A regular pentagon has one angle of 108°. What is the size of each of its other angles?
items.e: In a regular polygon all the angles are equal, so every angle is 108°.

items.q: Freya cuts a round cake into 4 equal slices from the centre. What angle does each slice make at the centre?
items.e: The slices go all the way round the centre: 360°. 360° ÷ 4 = 90°, a right angle. (45° comes from using 180°.)

items.q: Three paths meet at a point. Two of the angles between them are 90° and 150°. What is the third angle?
items.e: The three angles go all the way around the point: 360°. 90° + 150° = 240°, and 360° − 240° = 120°.

items.q: A regular octagon has a perimeter of 48 cm. How long is each side?
items.e: A regular octagon has 8 equal sides. 48 ÷ 8 = 6 cm.

c: Regular: all sides and all angles are equal
Irregular: the angles are not all equal
Irregular: the sides are not all equal
Irregular: the sides and the angles are not all equal
items.e: All 6 sides have the same mark and all 6 angles have the same mark. Equal sides and equal angles: regular.

items.q: The marks show which sides and angles are equal. Is this polygon regular or irregular?
c: Irregular: the sides are not all equal
Regular: all sides and all angles are equal
Irregular: the sides and the angles are not all equal
Irregular: the angles are not all equal
items.e: All 4 angles are right angles, but the long sides and the short sides are different. Equal angles are not enough, so this rectangle is irregular.

c: Irregular: the sides and the angles are not all equal
Irregular: the sides are not all equal
Irregular: the angles are not all equal
Regular: all sides and all angles are equal
items.e: All 4 sides are equal, but the angles are 60° and 120°. A regular polygon needs equal sides and equal angles, so this rhombus is irregular.

items.q: The minute hand turns clockwise from 12 to 9. How many degrees does it turn?
items.e: 12 to 3, 3 to 6 and 6 to 9 are three quarter turns: 3 × 90° = 270°. (90° is the short way, from 9 to 12.)

items.q: At 4 o’clock the smaller angle between the hands of a clock is 120°. What is the reflex angle between the hands?
items.e: The two angles between the hands go all the way round: 360°. 360° − 120° = 240°. (60° comes from using 180°.)

items.q: Which shape is always a regular polygon?
items.e: An equilateral triangle always has 3 equal sides and 3 equal angles (60° each). A rectangle, a rhombus or a hexagon can be irregular.

items.q: A robot faces north. It turns through 3 right angles clockwise. Which way does it face now?
items.e: Clockwise from north: east (1 right angle), south (2), west (3). (East would be 3 right angles anticlockwise.)

items.q: Evie draws a hexagon. All its angles are 120°, but some sides are 3 cm and some are 5 cm. Is it regular?
c: Yes, the angles are all equal
No, the sides are not all equal
No, the angles are not all equal
items.e: Regular needs equal angles and equal sides. The sides are 3 cm and 5 cm, so the hexagon is irregular.

items.q: A shape has 4 equal sides. Must it be a regular polygon?
c: Yes, all its sides are equal
No, its angles must be equal too
items.e: A regular polygon has all sides equal and all angles equal. A rhombus has 4 equal sides but its angles can be different.

items.q: Ethan measures an angle and writes 40°. The angle is clearly bigger than a right angle. What should he have written?
items.e: An angle bigger than a right angle is more than 90°. Ethan read the wrong scale: the other scale gives 180° − 40° = 140°.

items.q: Leo faces east in the playground. He turns 90° anticlockwise. Which way does he face now?
items.e: Anticlockwise from east, a quarter turn takes you to north. (Clockwise would be south.)

items.q: A windmill sail turns a half turn and then a quarter turn more. How many degrees does it turn altogether?
items.e: A half turn is 180° and a quarter turn is 90°. 180° + 90° = 270°.

items.q: A reflex angle and an angle of 85° fit together to make a whole turn. What is the reflex angle?
items.e: A whole turn is 360°. 360° − 85° = 275°. (95° comes from using 180°.)
